Okay, so I need to find the sum of all prime numbers less than 75. Hmm, primes are numbers greater than 1 that have no positive divisors other than 1 and themselves. So, I guess I need to list all the prime numbers below 75 and then add them up. 

First, let me recall what prime numbers are. They are numbers like 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, and so on. Each prime number is only divisible by 1 and itself. So, to approach this, I can start listing numbers from 2 upwards and check each one to see if it's prime. If it is, I'll add it to my running total.

But wait, listing all numbers up to 75 and checking each one might take a while. Maybe there's a smarter way to do this. I remember something called the Sieve of Eratosthenes, which is an ancient algorithm for finding all primes up to a certain limit. Maybe I can use that method here.

Let me try to remember how the Sieve of Eratosthenes works. You start by writing down all numbers from 2 up to the limit, which in this case is 75. Then, you start with the first number, 2, which is prime. You mark all multiples of 2 as non-prime. Then you move to the next number that isn't marked, which is 3, mark all its multiples, and continue this process until you've processed all numbers up to the square root of 75. The numbers that remain unmarked are the primes.

Okay, so let me try to apply this method. I'll list all numbers from 2 to 75. Then, starting with 2, I'll cross out every second number (4, 6, 8, etc.). Next, I'll move to 3 and cross out every third number (6, 9, 12, etc.), but I've already crossed out 6, so I'll start from there. Then I'll go to 5 and cross out every fifth number, and so on.

But wait, doing this manually might be time-consuming. Maybe I can list the primes as I go along instead. Let me try that.
